stem: A 14-year-old who has been taking chronic corticosteroid therapy for several months becomes acutely unwell while the steroid dose is being reduced; what is the most appropriate consideration?

options.text: Acute adrenal crisis should be considered, especially during stress or tapering
Adrenal crisis is only relevant if the child has atypical genitalia
Chronic corticosteroid exposure protects against adrenal insufficiency during illness
Tapering lowers adrenal risk because exogenous steroids are being withdrawn
Adrenal crisis should only be considered after failure to respond to antibiotics

explanation: Acute adrenal crisis should be considered in a child on chronic corticosteroids who becomes unwell during stress or steroid tapering.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because chronic corticosteroid exposure can suppress the adrenal axis, so acute illness or tapering can precipitate adrenal crisis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because atypical genitalia is not required to consider adrenal crisis in an older child with steroid exposure.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because chronic corticosteroid exposure increases, rather than removes, the risk of adrenal insufficiency during illness.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because tapering can unmask adrenal suppression and increase the risk of adrenal crisis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because adrenal crisis should be considered promptly on clinical grounds, not only after antibiotic failure.
